producer_report.summary: I wrote the squash-chain design (`docs/design/squash-chain-landing.md`) and decision D69. No Rust code, `athena.toml`, workflows or records were changed. The design recommends a chain-aware landing rule. Each job's `candidate.json` gains `base_fingerprint`. The gate accepts a commit adding several jobs' closing records when they form one linear chain. That means the first job's base fingerprint equals the parent's fingerprint, each later job's base equals the previous job's candidate fingerprint, and the last job's fingerprint equals the landed tree. Each job still passes the other per-job checks it passes today, including that its reading precedes its own work, so M23 is kept. The document also lists four rejected alternatives with tradeoffs, the exact check, refusal messages, and the follow-up work. `CHANGELOG.md` gains a line. `docs/design/athena-v0.md`, `docs/enforcement.md` and `docs/architecture.md` get short 'proposed, not in force' pointers. `cargo test --locked`, `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` all pass."

checks_run.note: all suites passed, including xtask policy tests (enforcement map, boundary scanner)

open_issues: The design is a proposal; the user must accept D69 before implementation.

Implementation follow-up: base_fingerprint field in Candidate and docs/records.md, core writing it, chain check in invariant.rs landing, landing_tests.rs cases, update of design §7.3 and enforcement.md.
Intermediate chain states are proved only by unsigned records, and pre-field jobs cannot form chains.
